items.excerpt: Three AI-driven startups (Spain's Alighieria with Publisher OS, Germany's Lit-X, and New Zealand's Narrative Muse) are pitching publishers on data-analytics tools that target different parts of the acquisition and marketing pipeline, promising data can inform decisions long driven by instinct without replacing editorial judgment.
items.note: Concrete new AI tools reshaping the acquisition/marketing workflow for publishers. Published 2026-07-10; FRESH. Not in books history.

items.excerpt: Take-a-Break's Fiction Feast magazine has told regular story contributors that 'AI tools will be used' on future in-house-created stories, signaling how a mass-market short-fiction outlet is changing the way it produces content.
items.note: Creative-AI workflow shift at a fiction publisher. Published 2026-07-10; FRESH. Not in history.

items.excerpt: Audiobook publisher Bolinda used interviews, archival research and human expertise to build an AI-generated voice replicating the late romance author Barbara Cartland, reviving a deceased author's distinctive narration for new audiobook editions.
items.note: AI voice-cloning applied to audiobook narration craft. Distinct from the 7/7 Michael Caine/ElevenLabs story. Published 2026-07-09; FRESH.

items.excerpt: A user discovered that text pasted from Claude into Archive of Our Own retains hidden markup flagging AI involvement, exposing popular fanfiction stories as AI-assisted despite anti-AI tags and dismaying the fan-writing community.
items.note: Creative-writing craft/community shift around AI-assisted fiction and detectability. Published 2026-07-08; FRESH. Distinct outlet for source diversity.
